reason: The verse makes the mind a bow (மனதை வில்லாக்கி) and awareness the arrow (அறிவை அம்பாக்கி), an image of concentrated attention, but it makes no claim about wandering or happiness, which is what the finding measures.

The verse calls the body a vessel made of clay from a pit of filth (ஊத்தைக் குழி) mixed in blood (உதிரப் புனல்), not worth a dry stick; it shares the topic of the body but makes no claim about its microbial make-up.
The verse places consciousness (சைதன்னியம்) above the three Vedantic cosmic selves; it shares the topic of consciousness with Orch-OR but says nothing about how consciousness arises physically.

reason: The verse urges joining the mind to its object as a magnet holds iron (காந்தம் இரும்பு) and holding on unwavering (சலியாமல் தொடர்ந்து) with calm; it shares the topic of sustained attention but makes no claim about how often minds wander or how that relates to happiness.
The verse names meditation and silence (தியானமான மோனமே) at the crown (உச்சி மத்தி) in a string of images, but states no claim about what meditation does that a DMN finding could test.
text_issue: செச்சி and கச்சி are rhyme words of unclear sense.

reason: The verse denies that any plant or root is a kalpa (செடிபூடு கற்பமில்லை) and says the body becomes firm by the subdued mind in Brahman; the finding concerns an herb lowering self-reported stress, which does not bear on the claim about bodily permanence.

The verse asks to regard other lives as one's own (தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி) and stop killing to eat, as the completion of tapas; it shares the theme of compassion but claims nothing about wellbeing or distress, which the finding measures.

The verse claims a red calcined product (செந்தூரம்) transmutes the nine metals (நவலோகம்) and gives the whole art of vedai; the finding is about heavy-metal poisoning from ingested preparations, which shares the topic of Siddha metal products but does not speak to the transmutation claim.

The verse laments maya, desire and the mind's scattering and points to the root (மூலம் பாரே); nothing in it concerns perception as the brain's prediction, and linking maya to predictive processing needs a gloss the Tamil does not give.

The verse lists the body as an oozing container, a leather bag of rice (சோறிடுந் தோற்பை) and a pot packed with wind (காற்றிற் பொதிந்த பாண்டம்); it shares the topic of the body but makes no claim about the bacteria it holds.

The belly (சோற்றுக் குழி) is made to say it will not yet be filled, the body's appetite speaking as a will; this shares the gut-and-behaviour topic but makes no claim about microbial signalling to the brain.

The verse says those who cannot bind the alkali (காரத்தைக் கட்ட) or calcine the salt (சாரத்தை நீற்றி) work in vain, a claim about the order of alchemical operations; it never names mercury or gold, so the transmutation finding only shares the alchemical topic.
The verse claims reciting the beginningless mantra in the heart (நெஞ்சிலே நினைந்து, செபிப்பீரேல்) makes great sins fly off like cotton; it says nothing about breath counts or lifespan.

The verse claims the body does not age (ஆக்கை மூப்பது இல்லையே) through folding the tongue and holding 'the pair' (இரட்டை); reading the pair as breaths is a gloss, the verse does not mention reciting, and the finding on recitation slowing breath does not address non-ageing.
The verse calls the body's pot a jar of excrement (மலச்சால்); it shares the topic of what the body contains but makes no claim the bacterial-cell count speaks to.

The verse is a narrative of the vel loosed against the asuras whose minds were not subdued (மனமடங்காத அசுரர்); the subdued mind is incidental to a myth and makes no claim about mind-wandering or happiness.
The verse longs to die before the body, the cage (கூண்டு), falls; the shared 'body' is incidental and the finding on bacterial cells has nothing to say about it.

The verse mocks alchemists who blow fumes (புகைத் தூது) without the key of vaadham (வாதக் திறவுகோல்); it shares the topic of mineral preparations but makes no claim about their safety or contents that the contamination finding tests.

The verse is about death's call (காலன் ஓசை) making houses and doors useless; it has nothing on fasting or autophagy.
The verse claims old deeds (வல்வினை) fly away when thought settles at the root (வேரிலே கருத்தொடுங்க); it has nothing about perception as prediction.
The verse asks whether worldly life can be left and the mind made firm without grace (நின்னருளின்றியே); it makes no claim about expectation or symptoms.

The verse speaks of an unreachable twelve-legged horse (புரவி) whose four legs are bound; reading the horse as breath is the cipher, not fixed by the Tamil, and even then binding is retention, not the slow paced breathing the HRV finding concerns.
The verse is an akam-style boast of a hero with bow and eagles (பருந்து) on a robber-infested road; it has nothing to do with metal poisoning.

reason: The verse calls the silent letter (மௌனாக்ஷரம்) the key that opens the way to the crown (உச்சிவழி); it shares the topic of silent mantra but the cortical-deactivation finding does not address the claim of opening a way to the crown.
The verse traces a path from ignorance (அஞ்ஞானம்) to true knowledge (மெய்ஞ்ஞானம்); it makes no claim about placebos or symptoms.

The verse is an alchemical procedure claiming to purify a substance (சாபந் தீர்த்தே) by sealing and firing (சீலை மண்); it names no metal and makes no health claim, so the poisoning finding only shares the topic of Siddha preparations.

reason: The verse speaks of eating the breath (வாசியை வாரி யுண்டோம்) and passing through the letters ம, வ, சி; reading these as recitation of the five-letter mantra is a gloss, and the verse makes no claim about breathing rate or baroreflex.

The verse reports pure space appearing as light and all as Brahman (சகலமும் பிரமமயம்), with சத்துச்சித்தானந்தம; it shares the topic of consciousness but Orch-OR's microtubule hypothesis does not bear on a claim of all-pervading Brahman.

The verse likens the sun and moon (கதிர் மதி) becoming one to the breath within the body (உயிர்ப்பு) the poet does not know; mapping sun and moon to nostrils is a cipher the line does not fix, and the verse makes no claim about hemispheres or autonomic tone.
The verse's one instruction is to be still (சும்மா இரு); it shares the topic of meditative stillness but claims only that the stillness is what was pointed to, nothing the DMN finding can test.

The verse claims a white kasa root (காசாம் வேர்) in the tank of Kayampatti and rising from the mouth-river makes the body not perish (உடல் மாயாது); reading the place as the body is a gloss, and an herb lowering stress does not bear on deathlessness.
The verse asks what learning or gain is worth to those who do not know the Lord (உன்னையறியாதார் உய்வரோ); it has nothing about perception or prediction.

The verse claims the freed mind stays in silence (மோனத்தே) whatever work is done, like the water carrier whose mind stays on the pot (நீர்க்குடம்); it shares the meditation topic but makes no claim the DMN finding addresses.
The verse mocks millions who call themselves jnani (ஞானிஞானி என்றுரைத்த நாய்கள்) and argue about impossibilities; it says nothing about mind-wandering or happiness.
The verse is an image of hunting the deer with the sky as bow and the five letters as arrow (ஐந்தெழுத்தை யம்பாக்கி); it has nothing on the body's cell turnover.

The verse calls the body a stinking pot filled with rice and curry (சோறுங் கறியும் நிரப்பிய பாண்டம்); it shares the topic of the body as container but makes no claim the bacterial-cell count speaks to.

The verse has the mind set at the suzhumunai (சுழுமுனை) at dawn while sun and moon (பரிதிமதி) exchange; reading them as alternating nostrils is a cipher not fixed by the Tamil, which names no breath, and the verse makes no claim about blood pressure.
